md: And it was. The letter vav (“and”) adds and connects to where the Torah ended — the account of Moshe’s death: after that the L-rd said to Joshua, etc.
My servant Moshe is dead. That is: had he still been alive, you could not have crossed the Jordan, for it was decreed that he would not cross.
And now. Since he has died — arise, cross, etc.
On which. This goes back to the start of the verse: every spot.
Where the sun sets. That is, on the side where the sun sets — the west.
No one shall stand. That is, no one will find the strength to stand up straight before you.
I will not fail you. I will not withdraw My support from you.
Be strong and resolute. In leading the people properly.
But, etc. For without this, nothing will help you lead the people properly.
That you may. Through keeping the Torah you will succeed.
This. The one spoken of in the previous verse (verse 7): “which Moshe enjoined upon you.”
So that you may observe. For if it departs from your lips, you may forget something.
Only then. When you take care to do, etc. — then you will prosper.
I charge you. I command you: be strong in war against the enemy and do not fear.

For the L-rd is with you, etc. It does not say “for I am with you,” though it was the L-rd Himself who was speaking. So too (I Samuel 12:11): “and He sent… and Shmuel,” though it was Shmuel himself who was speaking.

And charge, etc. Although this is told before the spies were sent, the command must have come after it: on the day the spies went they lodged in Jericho; they stayed three days in the hills; on their return they lodged in their own place; the next day they lodged by the Jordan, and the day after they crossed the Jordan.
Get ready. Although they still ate the manna, they also had produce of the land — what merchants of the nations brought them; this is what he told them to get ready.
Remember. You must remember.
Is granting you a haven. He gives you a place of rest by giving you this land on this side of the Jordan.
Until He grants a haven. Until the L-rd gives a place of rest to them too.
And possess it. That is: then you will hold it with no one disputing it, since you kept the condition.
Where the sun rises. On the eastern side.
Only, etc. That is: we will obey you only when the L-rd is with you, etc., but not otherwise.
Only be strong. To punish the rebels and not to forgive an affront to your honor.
Spies, secretly. To find out what the people were thinking — whether their hearts had melted.
Saying. That is, he said this.
And hid him. Each one in a separate place, for it is easier to hide them one by one.
The men. The ones you are asking about.
But I didn’t know. When they came.
When the gate. That is, when it was time to close the city gate, as it grew dark.
For you can overtake them. Since they left only a short while ago.
And hidden them. She hid them again, in a more hidden place.
Under stalks of flax. Under flax still on its stalks — the stems of the flax.
Laid out. So that no one would notice that someone was hidden there.
After them. So the pursuers thought.
Was shut. Since they wanted to keep searching for them in the city, the gatekeepers shut the gate, so that no one could leave from then on.
They. The spies.
Because dread has fallen, etc. And we have no strength to fight you.
And no spirit was left, etc. That is, everyone’s spirit sank low.
He is G-d. So He has power over them all.
Now. Since the matter is clear.
Loyalty. For you have not yet done me any good.
Show, etc. So you too show kindness to my father’s house, though they did you no good first.
A reliable sign. A true sign — so that all Israel will know not to harm us.
Our persons, etc. If anyone wants to harm you, we will give ourselves up to death to save you.
This mission of ours. The sign you ask for, which will be given to you: if you tell about the sign, many will use it to save themselves.
True loyalty. You did us a kindness but hoped for a reward; we will do you a true kindness, with no hope of reward.
Through the window. Because the city gates were shut.
In the wall. The window faced outward, beyond the city wall.
So that they may not come upon you. If you go your way now, the pursuers may meet you on their way back.
There. In the hills.
Released. That is, we want to be free of the sin of a broken oath, so let us explain the matter well.
We invade. That is, when we come into the land.
This. By which you let us down.
You tie. As a sign and a mark.
Through which. This refers to the window, meaning “by way of it.”
His blood will be on his head. That is, the guilt for his death is on himself — he brought it on himself.
And we shall be clear. For it would have been impossible to keep him from death.
This. This mark and this sign.
Let it be as you say. That is, this is the right way.
She sent them. They went to the hills on her advice, so it says “she sent them.”
And she tied. When Israel came into the land.
Has delivered. The previous verse says that they told all that had happened to them; when they finished telling, they said: here is the conclusion — the L-rd has delivered, etc.
There. By the Jordan.
Three days. As it says above (1:11): “in three days’ time,” etc.
The Ark of the Covenant of the L-rd. The Ark that holds the Tablets: when the L-rd gave them, He made a covenant with Israel.
You shall. Then you shall set out.
Between it. And the Ark.
Some two thousand. Exactly two thousand, since it says “by measure.” The letter kaf (“some”) stresses that it is exact, as in (Genesis 25:31) “sell me this day.”
So that, etc. This goes back to the previous verse: follow the Ark so that you may know the way, since you have never traveled it.
For tomorrow, etc. wonders. So it is fitting to be holy then, and pure of impurity.
So that they shall know. Through the wonders I will do through you.
The edge. Its western edge.
Make a halt in the Jordan. And do not step out onto dry land at once.
By this. By the wonder he goes on to describe.
The Sovereign, etc. That is, “the Ark of the Sovereign,” etc.
Select. So that they, in place of all of you, would stand near the Ark and see that as soon as the priests’ feet came to rest, the waters would be cut off at once.

When the feet come to rest. This goes back to what was said above: they will see that as soon as the priests’ feet come to rest, the water now coming down from upstream will be cut off at once and flow away.
Will stand. The water that comes afterwards to the place where it was cut off will stand there in a single heap.
At its edge. On the eastern side.

The Jordan keeps flowing over its entire bed. This shows how great the miracle was: although the Jordan has much water — even all through the harvest, when rivers usually run low, it was full to its banks.
Piled up. This goes back to what was said above: with all that water, what came down from upstream, after it was cut off, stopped and rose in a single heap.
A great way off. That heap was very far from the town called Adam, which is next to Zarethan.
And those flowing away. The water that flowed down before it was cut off, toward the Sea of the Arabah — the Dead Sea.
Ran out completely. That water ran out of its place entirely and flowed away, and the place was left dry.
Stood. They did not leave the Jordan at once, but stood on the western side until all had crossed, as he had commanded.
Firmly. That is, they stood ready and steady, fixed in place, until all had crossed.
From the middle of the Jordan. He told them to go back to the edge of the Jordan after they had come out of it.
From the spot where they stand. From the place where the priests stood firmly: they lifted their feet, and the men took the stones that were under them.
Whom he had designated. To stand near the Ark and see that as soon as the priests’ feet came to rest, the waters would be cut off, as written above (3:13).
In the middle of the Jordan. For they had already come out of it, as said (verse 1).
A symbol. A sign to remember.
In time to come. That is, after some time.
Twelve, etc. These were other stones (Sotah 35b). “To this day” means forever: whoever reads this verse in his own time says “to this day.” This is an important rule in the words of the prophets.

To convey to the people. Our Sages of blessed memory said (Sotah 34a): G-d commanded him to tell the people, “Know that you are crossing the Jordan on dry land on condition that you drive out all the inhabitants of the land.” And Moshe had commanded him that very thing.
Speedily. Out of respect for the Ark, which stood until they had crossed.
The Ark of the L-rd advanced. After Joshua told the priests to come up out of the Jordan, as written below (verse 17), the Ark crossed over to go before the people.
At the instance of the L-rd. That is, on the mission of the Omnipresent.
And you shall fear. Meaning “and so that you shall fear”: the letter vav is missing, and there are many such cases.
And no spirit was left, etc. Said as an overstatement: as if the spirit of life had left them from their great fear.
A second circumcision, etc. It says “second” because on the night they left Egypt, too, all Israel was circumcised together; so said our Sages of blessed memory (Bamidbar Rabbah 11:6).
At Gibeath. At the Hill of Foreskins; the place was named after what happened there.
This is the reason. That is, this is why Joshua alone circumcised the whole people, and they did not circumcise one another then: how could it be that none of them knew how to circumcise?
All the people. That is, all the people who came out of Egypt — who were circumcised and fit to circumcise others — had died in the wilderness, and none were left to circumcise the rest.
Had been circumcised. That is, only the people who came out were circumcised, but not those born in the wilderness, so they were not fit to circumcise others.
Until the entire nation had perished, etc. So none of the circumcised was left who was fit and suited to circumcise others.
Had sworn. Because of this the L-rd swore to them that they would not, etc.
He had raised up in their stead. That is, “whom He had raised up in their stead.”

These Joshua circumcised. They had not been circumcised until then — they were uncircumcised up to that time, for those who came out of Egypt did not circumcise their sons on the way. So apart from Joshua there was no circumcised man fit and suited to circumcise others.

Today I have rolled away. Now I have removed from you the taunt of the Egyptians, who said, “Why, they are uncircumcised like us!” For Israel this is a disgrace, as it is written (Genesis 34:14): “for that is a disgrace to us.”
Toward evening. After midday it is called “evening,” for then the sun inclines toward the west.
On the day after the passover. On the day after the first day of Pesach, which is the time of bringing the Omer: they brought the Omer and then ate.

The manna ceased. Although the manna stopped falling on the day Moshe died, the seventh of Adar, they were miraculously fed from the manna left in their vessels; once they ate of the produce of the land, they found no more of it.
They ate. They began to eat.
Near Jericho. That is, within the bounds of Jericho.
Are you one of us. The letter hei here asks a question: have you come to help us against the enemy, or to help the enemy?

He replied, “No.” That is: I have not come to help Israel’s enemies, for I am the captain of Israel, who are called the L-rd’s host. And you have not seen me until now because I have come only now, and not before.
What does my lord command. That is: say your words and I am ready to carry them out, as a servant carries out his master’s words.
Is holy. And it is fitting to stand on it barefoot.

Shut up tight. That is, it had always been closed with doors and bolt, and now they closed it even more because of Israel and let no one leave or enter, so that the ways into the city would not become known.
Warriors. That is, even though they are mighty warriors.
Do this. Go around once a day.
Blowing. Every day, when they go around.
That sound. That is, the sound drawn out in a long blast.
Every man straight ahead. They will not need to go around and climb it, for the whole wall will fall.
When Joshua had instructed. That is, they did just as Joshua told the people, and the seven, etc.
Blowing the horns. This refers to the priests.
Sounding all the time. That is, the priests did not stand still while blowing, but walked and blew.
Rose early. On the second day.
Blowing as they marched. Repeated to say that they never stopped blowing.
At daybreak. So that there would be enough time to go around seven times.
Only, etc. That is why they had to rise earlier then than on the other days.
Blew. That is, a drawn-out, long blast.
Proscribed. For destruction and cutting off.
It, etc. That is, the city itself and whatever in it is not fit to be brought into the treasury of the L-rd.
For the L-rd. That is, for the sake of the L-rd’s name and His honor.
Beware. Guard yourselves and others from taking anything of what is proscribed.
Or else you will be proscribed, if you take, etc. Lest you cut off Israel by what you take of the proscribed, for all would perish; this is “you will cause the camp to be proscribed,” etc.
All the silver, etc. These are the things fit for the treasury of the L-rd.
So the people shouted. And it goes on to explain: when the people heard the sound of the horn — when it is drawn out in a long blast — then they shouted.
Pronounced this oath. A curse is called an oath.

He shall lay its foundations at the cost of his first-born. When he lays the foundation, his firstborn son will die; the rest will die while the building goes on; and when he sets up the gates, his youngest son will die. So all of them will die.
Violated, etc. Because they did not watch over one another, Scripture counts it as if all of them had violated it.
Not all need go up. That is, there is no need for all of them.
If only we had been content. Had we only wanted then to stay on the eastern side of the Jordan and not cross the Jordan, this trouble would not have come upon us.
What can I say. Sensing that he had said too much against the L-rd’s deed, he spoke again: what can I say if not this, since Israel has turned tail in flight? And I cry out from the pain of my heart.
Will hear. That the enemy is pursuing them.
And what will You do about Your name. So that it will not be profaned when they say, “They perished because the L-rd was unable.”
Why, etc. That is, there is no need for prayer, only to remove the one who violated the proscription.
Israel has sinned. Although one man sinned, still, because they did not watch over one another, Scripture counts it as if all of them had sinned.

They have broken My covenant. This comes to stress how great that outrage was: even one who sins against another person will not go unpunished, and they did not fear and broke My covenant — they violated the proscription, which is like an oath.
They have taken. That is, even one who transgresses any other of the L-rd's commandments will surely be punished, and they even took from what was consecrated to the Most High, the L-rd's portion.

They have stolen. Had they taken it in front of everyone, they would at least have treated the honor of the Omnipresent like the honor of a human being of flesh and blood; but they stole, hiding from people, and did not fear the L-rd.
They have broken faith. A thief is not despised if he repents, confesses and returns what he took, but they even denied it.

And put it in their vessels. That is (Proverbs 6:30): “A thief is not despised for stealing to appease his hunger,” but they even put it in their vessels to keep it as treasure, not to use it to satisfy their hunger. So that outrage was double and many times over.
For they have become proscribed. That is, they helped the one who violated the proscription by looking away and not watching over one another.
What is proscribed. The one who violated the proscription.
Purify yourselves. To pass before the Ark, to find out on whose account this trouble came.
You shall present yourselves. Before the Ark.
By tribes. Each tribe separately.
That the L-rd indicates (lit. “captures”). It will be “captured” before the Ark, so that for a while it cannot move from its place.
Shall come forward by clans. After they are moved from their place, they will come forward again by clans.
By ancestral houses. For the clan is further divided into ancestral houses.
Man by man. Individual men.
He who is indicated for proscription. The one who is “captured” before the Ark because he misappropriated the proscribed.
The clans of Judah. The tribe, too, is called a clan.
Man by man. Each man the head of an ancestral house.
And Zabdi was indicated. He was the head of the ancestral house.
Man by man. Individual men.
Honor to the L-rd. For when they see that you were indicated justly, it will be honor to the L-rd.
And make confession to Him. Admit that it is true that you misappropriated the proscribed.
What you have done. That is, what things you took from the proscribed.

This is what I did (lit. “like this and like this”). Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 42b) that he said: I did this before, too — something like this in the war against the Canaanite and in the war against Midian; for in the war against the Canaanite, too, it is said (Numbers 21:2): “I will proscribe their towns,” and in Midian, too, they gave the gold as holy to the L-rd.
They are. The mantle and the wedge of gold.
Under it. Under the mantle.
Who hurried. So that Achan's relatives would not take the things to cover up their disgrace.
And displayed them. That is, they spread them out before the Ark, so that everyone would see that it was true.
With him. They went with Joshua.

And brought them up. Although they went to a valley, it says “brought up,” for before they reached the valley they went up by a mountain road to the valley, which was called “the Valley of Achor” (“of calamity”) after what happened.
What calamity you have brought upon us. That is, what great calamity you have brought upon us — and for this the L-rd will bring calamity upon you.

And stoned them. His sons and daughters and his ox, etc. (Perhaps because his sons and daughters knew of it, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 44a), and did not reveal it, they too were stoned. However, our Sages, of blessed memory, did not say so.)
They put them to the fire. The mantle, the wedge and the tent, etc.
Over him. Over his grave.
Which is still there. That is, it stands forever in its size.
That is why, etc., as is still the case. That is, it still has that name.
Do not be frightened. Since they had already fallen at this place, he was afraid to approach it again; therefore He told him, “Do not be frightened.”

All the fighting troops. He commanded that all these preparations and stratagems be made to mislead the nations, so that they would think that the whole victory came from the size of the army and the stratagems, and not that the hand of the L-rd had done this. Because of this they would all gather together, so that they too would be a large army and could devise plans and stratagems with many advisers. And this would be good for Israel, for they would strike them all at once, without needing to go from city to city to strike them.
Behind it. Not from the side from which you will approach it.
On the alert. To move quickly when needed.
We will flee. In order to mislead them.
They will come. And then they will come out to pursue us.
Until we have drawn them. That is, the flight will help until we draw them away from the city to pursue us, for they will say that we are really fleeing out of fear, as in the first battle.
While we are fleeing. And we will keep on fleeing, to draw them away from the city.
From your ambush. From the place where you will lie in ambush.
The city. Those who remain in the city.
As the L-rd has commanded. Who commanded that it be burned, as is written above (verse 2): “You shall treat Ai as you treated Jericho.”
Mind, I have given you your orders. That is, be careful and do not disobey my word.
Mustered. He checked whether they were ready for battle.
And stationed them as an ambush. He set yet another ambush, closer to the city.
Thus the army was disposed. The people themselves prepared the camp for battle, etc., and also prepared its far end — that is the ambush.
In the valley. To come closer to the city.
To the meeting place (lit. “to the appointed time”). At the same time at which they had gone out in the first battle.
As though routed. They made themselves look as if they were “stricken,” that is, beaten and weakened.
Gathered. They gathered at the call of the one who summoned them.
Hold out the javelin. To give a sign to the ambush to come into the city.
The pursuers. These are the men of Ai, who at first had been pursuing Israel.
The other. The men of the ambush.
And put it to the sword. The women and children.

A copy of the Teaching of Moses. The book “These are the words” (Deuteronomy) is called “Mishneh Torah” (the Repetition of the Torah), for in it is said a second time what was said in the four books before it.
Facing the levitical priests. The priests, sons of Levi, who stood with the Ark in the middle and said the blessing and the curse.
Half of them. Six tribes.

To bless, etc., of old (lit. “first”). (Mishnah, Sotah 7:5): First they began and said, “Blessed is the man who does not make a sculptured image, etc.,” and after this they said, “Cursed is the man, etc.,” and so with all the curses.
He read. Joshua was the one who read, as is written in the next verse.

All the words of the Teaching. And it goes on to explain that he read the blessing and the curse, just as is written in the Torah: these are the passages (Deuteronomy 28:1) “If you obey…” and “If you do not obey…,” said in the portion Ki Tavo, and others like them.
There was not a word. Of the blessing and the curse.
That Moses had commanded. That is, what is said in the Torah.
Learned of this. That they had captured Ai with a large force and by a stratagem.
They gathered. So that they too would have a large force and many advisers, to outwit Israel in the war.

Jericho and Ai. That is, these were two opposite things: Jericho was captured by a miracle, and Ai by stratagems and a large force. From this they understood that the trick had been done to mislead them, as said above (chapter 8).
They for their part resorted to cunning. As Israel had done.

In disguise. They made themselves look like envoys coming from a distant land, for the word “tzir” is used for an envoy sent far away, as it is written (Isaiah 57:9): “and you sent your envoys (tzirayich) far off.”
Worn-out. To mislead Israel into thinking they had worn out from the great length of the road.
Patched. Tied together around the cracks.
Patched. For when shoes grow old, they change and take on several colors.
Crumbly. For when bread grows old, it becomes moldy, with white, green and black spots on it.
From a distant land. Not from the land of Canaan, about which you were commanded (Deuteronomy 20:16): “you shall not let a soul remain alive.” Therefore make a pact with us to let us live.
Among us. Within the land given to me, which is the land of Canaan.

We will be your subjects. As if to say: we have no business with all this people, for we will be servants not to all of them, but to you alone. As if to say: and my lord will surely understand that we are not from the land of Canaan.
Who are you. From which people.
And where. From which country.
A very distant country. So you will not recognize either the people or the country.
Because of the fame of the L-rd. Because the Name of the L-rd has become famous.
We will be your subjects. To pay tribute.
Make a pact with us. To let us live.
This bread of ours. That you see in our hands: while it was still hot we took it as provision for the road.
See how dry. Because of the long time, from the great length of the road.
New. When they were filled, they were new.
Took. That is, they took proof from the dryness of their provisions and believed them. Or: they took from their provisions and ate, to seal the pact and the friendship.
This. That is, this thing — sparing their lives — we will do for them against our will, so that the L-rd will not be angry about breaking the oath.
The chieftains declared, “They shall live!” That is, because of the oath you must not say that they shall not live; but let us consider what to do with them as a requital for the deceit.
And they became etc. That is, the requital was that they became hewers etc., as the chieftains decreed, for the whole community obeyed them.
Therefore. That is, now, in the time of war, be accursed — slaves to the whole community; but to the House of the L-rd you will be slaves forever, and this will never cease.
And he did so. As he had said: to be slaves to the whole community in the time of war, and to the House of the L-rd forever.
From being killed. As they had thought at first.
For the community and for the altar etc., as they still are. That is, for the community in the time of war, and for the altar of the L-rd to this day.
In the place. Wherever the altar would stand, there they would serve — whether in Shiloh or in Jerusalem.
Remained among them. They joined themselves to Israel.
A large city. And even so they had no strength to fight, and by this they made the hearts of the warriors melt.
It has come to terms. And they did harm, for they brought fear into everyone’s heart.
Do not fail. By leaving us in their hands.
All night. So that they would not notice, and he would come upon them by surprise.
The Beth-horon ascent. On the road that goes up to Beth-horon.
To Azekah. For they fled by that road, and they pursued them and struck them along the road as far as Azekah etc.
Down the descent. As they went down the slope of the mountain.
Stones. Hailstones.
All the way to Azekah. Along the whole way they fled, from the descent of Beth-horon until they reached Azekah, the hailstones fell on them.
More. Greater in number.
Addressed the L-rd. In the Name of the L-rd and as His messenger.
He said. This is the same speech mentioned above; because he interrupted with other words, he said again “he said.”

Stand still, O sun, at Gibeon. For at that time the sun stood opposite Gibeon, and he feared it would set at its time and they would not be able to pursue the enemy in the darkness of night. Therefore he told the sun not to go on its way, but to wait longer opposite Gibeon, in the place where it stood.

O moon, in the Valley of Aijalon. For by then the moon had already risen and stood opposite the Valley of Aijalon, and he told it to wait in its place too and not go on its way. Perhaps he feared that if the moon went on its way, it would come opposite the sun, where the sun stood, and darken the sun’s light.
And the sun stood still. That is, so it was: the sun and the moon stood in their places.
While a nation wreaked judgment. Until Israel had finished taking vengeance on its enemies.

As is written. This thing is written as a promise in the Book of Jashar, which is the Torah, where it is said about Ephraim (Genesis 48:19): “and his offspring shall fill the nations.” This was the day the sun and the moon stood still for Joshua, who came from his offspring, and the whole world was filled with his fame.
Thus the sun halted. Now it explains the place where it stood.
In midheaven. That is, as it appeared on that horizon.
Did not press on to set. It did not hurry to set, as it always hurries to the place of its setting, moving on without stopping.
For a whole day. That is, it was held back, standing in one place, for the length of a full day, which is twenty-four hours.
Such a day. In which there was such a wonder — that He acted on etc., as He acted on the voice of Joshua to stop the sun and the moon.
For the L-rd. This wonder was done because the L-rd fought for Israel, and for their sake He did it.
Then Joshua returned. After all the events told in the verses that follow.
Roll large stones. So that they would not suddenly come out and flee.
Harass them from the rear. Kill those who go at the end of the army.
They were wiped out. For those who remained were very few, and it was as if all of them had perished.
Some fugitives who escaped. Those who remained of them came to the fortified towns.
No one so much as snarled etc. at a man. That is, even against a single man, when he was alone, no one moved his tongue to say anything bad, for the fear of them fell on everyone.
To this very day. That is, they lie there to this very day, meaning forever.
Its king. Perhaps they had made another king over themselves, for above it says that Joshua had put the king of Hebron to death.
All its towns. The towns near it.
At a single stroke. Since he did not capture Ai at one time, it says that all these he captured at one time.
Then Joshua returned. This is the same return that was mentioned above (verse 15).
At the foot of Hermon. Below Mount Hermon.
In the land of Mizpah. Mount Hermon was in the land of Mizpah.
Misrephoth-maim. Ditches in which sea water collects; the sun dries it up and it turns into salt.
Hazor was formerly, etc. That is why he began with it.
On their mounds. That is, at their full height: their walls did not fall during the conquest.
The hill country of Israel. Where our father Israel lived; it is called by his name.
Mount Halak. It was divided (nechlak) in two, one part here and one part there.
Which ascends. Which goes up as far as Seir.
Without quarter. From the Israelites.
Wiped out. For He stiffened their hearts in order to wipe them out.

From Hebron. Although it was Caleb who drove the Anakites out of Hebron, it is credited to Joshua, because it happened in his days, and every victory in war is credited to the one who commands the army.
According to their tribal divisions. According to the division described below.
Tribal. Each tribe received a separate share.
The Wadi Jabbok. The name of a place near the wadi; it was on the border of the Ammonites.
The eastern Arabah. It too was part of Sihon’s rule.
Southward. And on the south side he ruled below the slopes of Pisgah.
The territory of King Og, etc. That is, they also took possession of Og’s territory.
The border of King Sihon. Next to Sihon’s border, for the other half of Gilead belonged to Sihon.
The king of Jericho, one. This continues the verse before (verse 7): “And the following are the local kings,” etc., the king of Jericho, etc.
The king of Jokneam in the Carmel. Jokneam is the name of the royal city; it was near the city of Carmel and counted as part of it. So too “the king of Dor,” etc., and “the king of Goiim,” etc.

Old, advanced in years. “Old” is said of what one sees in a person: white hair and a wrinkled face; and sometimes this comes before its time. So the verse explains: “advanced in years,” as if to say, old age came in its proper time, according to the number of days.
Very much. And you will not be able to conquer all of it in your lifetime.
Are accounted Canaanite. And I gave the land of the Canaanites to Israel.
And those of the Avvim. They are not Philistines.
I Myself will dispossess. After your death I will drive them out before them.
Apportion their lands by lot. Cast lots among them, for what they have already conquered and for what they have not conquered yet, and each tribe will conquer its share.
As I have commanded you. As it is written (Deut. 3:28): “Give Joshua his instructions,” etc., “he shall allot it to them.”
Therefore, divide. That is, first divide the land into nine and a half parts, as the number of tribes receiving a share, and then cast lots to know which part is whose.

Along with the other half-tribe. That is, together with the second half of the tribe of Menashe, the Reubenites and the Gadites took their share (although the second half of the tribe of Menashe is not mentioned above, it says “with him,” since one half was mentioned). “As assigned to them by Moshe” refers to “had already received,” meaning: from the time Moshe gave it to them, they took that share and agreed to it; so the matter is settled, and nothing more is to be given to them on that side.
The fire offerings of the L-rd. The holy portions of the altar, which are given after the parts that make them permitted have been offered on the fire.
Concerning them. Lit. “to him”: to Moshe.
For their various clans. That is, Moshe did not give it to them all together for them to divide among themselves; he himself divided a share to each clan.
In the hill of the valley. On the hill that stood in the middle of the valley.
Who had dwelt in the land. Of the inhabitants of Sihon’s land.
Together with the others that they slew. Together with the rest of the slain and like them: he could not save himself with his sorcery.
The edge of the Jordan. That is, the edge of the Jordan too — the towns near the Jordan — were counted in Reuben’s territory.
For their various clans. Divided to each clan as a separate share.
To the descendants of Machir. Part of Gilead, etc., he gave to the descendants of Machir — not to all of them, but to half of the descendants of Machir.
Those, then, were the portions. These are the tribes to which Moshe gave a portion.
The L-rd, the G-d of Israel, etc. That is, what remains of the fire offerings of the L-rd is their portion.
And these. That is, these are the towns listed at the end of the account.
The portions that fell to them by lot. By lot he divided their portions to them.

For the portion … had been assigned. He explains why Joshua divided the land for nine and a half tribes. He says: although Moshe gave to two and a half tribes, and did not give a portion to the Levites — for none is to be given them, as the L-rd commanded — so that only eight and a half tribes were left deserving a portion, Joshua nevertheless had to divide the land for nine and a half tribes.

For whereas the descendants of Joseph. That is, since the descendants of Yosef were divided into two tribes, there were nine and a half besides the Levites; but neither Moshe nor Joshua gave a portion to the Levites.
To live in. That is, only to dwell in them, not that they should belong to them completely.
Just as the L-rd had commanded. Not to give a portion to the Levites.
When they apportioned. They divided it among themselves and gave none of it to the Levites.
The Judites approached. To help Caleb with his request.
Concerning you and me. That we would live and enter the land and not die in the wilderness.
A forthright report. Lit. “as was in my heart”: for with his mouth he agreed with the other spies, because he was afraid of them, but when he came before Moshe he contradicted them.
My companions. All the spies took the heart out of the people.
I was loyal. I held fully to the word of the L-rd.

Promised on oath. The Hebrew “if not” is an expression of an oath, as if he said: if this does not happen, then such and such will be the punishment — but the punishment is left unsaid; and so (Job 1:11): “if he does not blaspheme You to Your face.”
The land on which your foot trod. This is Hebron, as it says (Num. 13:22): “and he came to Hebron”; Caleb alone came to Hebron.
When Israel was journeying. During those years.

I am still as strong today. Since he came to ask for Hebron, he feared that Joshua might answer: “You have grown old and your strength is gone — how will you conquer Hebron?” So he said: I am still as strong as then.
My strength is the same now as it was then. The strength I had then is the strength I have today, both to fight myself and to go out and come in before the people to teach them the strategies of war.
This hill country. This is Hebron.
On that day. When we went to spy out the land.
That Anakites are there. And who has the strength to fight them?
If only the L-rd is with me. Perhaps the L-rd will be with me to conquer and drive them out, as He promised to give it to me.
Joshua blessed. That he should succeed in fighting them.
Hebron. The fields of the city and its villages; but the city itself was a city of refuge, and it and its pastures belonged to the kohanim, as is written below.
Thus. That is, it did not come to him as his share and lot among his family and tribe; it became his share for this reason, and he explains again: “because he was loyal,” etc.
Kiriath-arba. The city of a man named Arba, who was the great man among the Anakites; that is, even among the Anakites he was counted great and tall.
And the land had rest from war. As if to say: although this is written here after all the wars, it happened during the time of the war, and afterwards the land had rest from war.
To the various clans. What they divided by their clans; perhaps each clan received its own share, and they were not mixed with one another.
Down to the border of Edom. To receive their portion next to the border of Edom, which lay to the south of the Land of Israel.

Which is the Wilderness of Zin. That is, the Wilderness of Zin was the southern border of Judah; and he explains again, “at the far end of the south”: the Wilderness of Zin did not run the whole length of the southern border, but lay at the far end of the south, and from it the southern border began.
Their southern boundary. The southern border, from east to west.
From the tip of the Dead Sea. Which lay on the east of the Land of Israel; and there the Wilderness of Zin began.
From the tongue. Of that sea.

It proceeded. That border went outward to grow wider and came to the place south of the Ascent of Akrabbim; so the Ascent of Akrabbim was inside the border and counted as Judah’s. (Wherever it says “proceeded,” it means the border line went outward, the portion grew wider and continued from there in that width; wherever it says “made a turn” or “curved,” it means the border line went around that place only and then returned to the former width, or that one side ended and it turned to another side. And wherever it says “ran on,” it means either that the border ended there completely, or that the former width ended there, for from there on the portion became narrower — as can be seen on a drawing.) “Passed on to Zin” — from there the border passed to Zin, for the letter hei at the end stands for the letter lamed at the beginning. (Wherever it says “passed,” it means on straight, level ground; wherever it says “ascended,” that it went up a hill; wherever it says “descended,” that it went down a hill.) “To the south of Kadesh-barnea” — so it too belonged to the portion of the Judites.
The boundary ran on. The end of the border reached the Mediterranean Sea; so the border of Judah took up the whole length of the Land of Israel from east to west.
That shall be your. That is, this border will be the southern border from east to west for all Israel, as was said.
The boundary on the east. From south to north.
The Dead Sea. The border ran along the whole length of the sea, across the width of all its portion.

Up to the mouth of the Jordan. To its southern end, which falls into the sea. (From there, however, the Jordan ran along the south side westward and fell into the Mediterranean Sea — so said our Sages of blessed memory (Bechorot 55a). This explains what is written (Gen. 13:11): “Lot journeyed eastward” — although he turned west, to the plain of the Jordan on the west; and what is written (Gen. 50:10): “they came … beyond the Jordan,” meaning beyond the Jordan on the west, for they had no need to go by way of the eastern side of the Jordan.)
On the northern side. From east to west.
At the tongue of the Sea. Which faces north; and that is at the end of the Jordan, which faces south.
Beth-hoglah. That is, on its north side, as mentioned in the borders of Benjamin.

North of, etc. So Beth-arabah was inside the border and counted as Judah’s. (And although Beth-arabah is listed in the portion of Benjamin, one must say that there were two places with one name, and one had an additional name to tell them apart, which is not mentioned in Scripture; and so one must say wherever the name of one place is mentioned two or three times, whether in the portion of one tribe or of two tribes.)
From the Valley of Achor. For from the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben the border came to the Valley of Achor; although this is not said, it is understood by itself.

And turned north. When the border came opposite Gilgal, the border line widened and went out to the north to Gilgal, which faces the Ascent of Adummim; that ascent stands south of the wadi; and the border went from Gilgal straight to the Ascent of Adummim, and the wadi was outside the border line, not within Judah’s border.
The boundary continued. From the Ascent of Adummim.
And ran on, etc. North of En-rogel was the end of the border at this width, and from there the border line went inward and the portion grew narrower.

Then the boundary ascended. From En-rogel the border went inward, toward the south, and climbed the hill to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, which lay on the south side of Jerusalem. (Jerusalem itself belonged to the portion of Benjamin, but a strip went out of the portion of Judah and came into Jerusalem, Zevachim 54b.) And it says “ascended,” for Jerusalem was higher than all the Land of Israel, except for Ein Eitam.
That is, Jerusalem. This is said of the Jebusites.

The boundary then ran up to the top of the hill. It still rises up to the fountain of the Waters of Nephtoah, which is Ein Eitam, mentioned by our Sages of blessed memory (Zevachim 54b). “On the west” — the hill was west of the Valley of Ben-hinnom and at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim; so the valley was within Judah’s border.
Ran on to the towns of Mount Ephron. That is, on the northern side, and they belonged to Judah.
Westward. Toward the west.
North of. So Mount Jearim, that is Chesalon, was inside the border and belonged to Judah.
The northern flank. And Ekron was inside the border.
The boundary ran on. The end of the border reached the Mediterranean Sea.
The western boundary. The western border, from north to south.
The Mediterranean Sea. The Great Sea was the border.
The edge. That is, the islands of the sea were also counted in Judah’s border and were its portion.
On all sides. That is, surrounding the portion of all their clans.
In accordance with the L-rd’s command. That is, Joshua did not give it to Caleb on his own, but by the word of the L-rd.
The father of Anak. That is, Arba was the father of Anak, meaning the greatest among the Anakites.
When she came. To her husband’s house.
She induced him. She persuaded her husband and coaxed him to let her ask her father for a field herself.
She dismounted from her donkey. She threw herself from the donkey to fall to the ground.
What is the matter? What do you lack, that you want to ask for it?
For you have given me away as Negeb-land. The field you gave me earlier is dry land, without springs of water.
So give me. For this I ask that you give me a field with a spring of water.
Upper and Lower Gulloth. He gave her a field with a spring above and a spring below.
By their clans. Divided to each clan separately.
At the far end. Those standing at the edge of Judah’s portion, next to the border of Edom, in the south of Judah.

Hazor-hadattah, etc. There are four towns in this verse: Hazor is the first, Hadattah the second, Kerioth the third, and Hezron, which is Hazor, the fourth. This is not the Hazor mentioned at the beginning of the verse, nor the one in the verse before it (verse 23).

29 towns. When you count them one by one you will find thirty-eight; this is because nine of them did not remain with the Judites, for the Simeonites took them from Judah’s portion, and they are listed in the portion of the Simeonites: Beer-sheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual, Ezem, Eltolad, Hormah, Ziklag, Ain and Rimmon.
With their villages. And besides their villages.
Gederah, and Gederothaim. This is one town, called by both names.

Zenan, etc. These too stood in the Lowland, but in another district; so he counted these by themselves and those by themselves. And so one should say wherever he counts these separately and those separately.
Gederoth, Beth-dagon. These are two towns: one is Gederoth, the other Beth-dagon.
From Ekron westward, etc. From Ekron toward the west, all the towns near Ashdod belonged to Judah, and also the villages of those towns.
All the way to the Wadi of Egypt. Which was to the south of Judah.
The Mediterranean Sea. That is, and up to the Great Sea, which was to its west.
The edge. The border of the sea too — the islands in the sea — were counted as part of Judah’s portion.
Ziph. This is not the Ziph mentioned above (verse 24).
The Jebusites. The name of the nation.
The Judites could not dispossess. For they too had some part in Jerusalem together with the Benjaminites, as our Sages of blessed memory said (Zevachim 53b): a strip went out from Judah’s share, etc.

To the Josephites. These are Manasseh and Ephraim; they took land next to each other, but each took a separate share; and their portion too filled the whole length of the Land of Israel from east to west, like the portion of Judah.
From the Jordan at Jericho. From the Jordan opposite Jericho the border began to run and came to the east of the waters of Jericho; this is the southern border, from east to west.
From Jericho it ascended. That is, from the waters of Jericho it went up into the wilderness and came to the hill country of Bethel. This is not the Bethel that is called Luz.
To Luz. That is, south of Luz, as is written of the border of Benjamin.
Westward. Toward the west.
As far as the border, etc. That is, south of Lower Beth-horon.
Ran on. The end of the border reached the Mediterranean Sea.
Received their portion. In that strip Manasseh and Ephraim received their portion.
By their clans. Of the portion divided among all their clans.
On the east. The boundary of the width facing east ran from Atroth-addar, which stood north of Benjamin, as far as

Upper Beth-horon, which stood in the portion of Ephraim. And since from Upper Beth-horon the border extended further to the west, as is written in this passage, there was also a boundary of width there; so it says “on the east,” meaning the boundary of width facing east, not the one facing west.
And the boundary ran on to the Sea. From Upper Beth-horon the border went on, extending further to the west, north of Michmethath, which was in the portion of Manasseh.

The boundary proceeded. In width, toward the north, to the east of Taanath-shiloh, and it passed along the whole length of Taanath-shiloh, not right next to it but east of Janoah, which stood east of Taanath-shiloh; and neither Taanath-shiloh nor Janoah was in Ephraim’s portion — they were in Manasseh’s.
It descended. For there the width ended, and from there it went down eastward to Ataroth.
Touched on Jericho. The border touched Jericho, that is, the waters of Jericho, passed through them, and ended at the Jordan.

From Tappuah. It stood by the Jordan within the border of Manasseh, but it belonged to Ephraim, as is written in this passage; from it the border ran westward and came to the Wadi Kanah from the south and ended at the Sea; the next verse explains what this border is.
This. That is, the border described in the previous verses, around the portion of the tribe of the Ephraimites divided to each clan.

The towns marked off. That is, the towns of the Ephraimites that were separated and set apart from the border of their portion stood within the portion of the Manassites, on the border described in the previous verse.
All those towns. Which stood along that border — they and their villages belonged to the Ephraimites.
They failed to dispossess. This refers to the Ephraimites, for Gezer was in their portion, one of the towns on the border that runs from Tappuah to the Sea.
Forced labor. That is, not a tax of money but a tax of bodily labor.

For he was Joseph’s first-born. That is, although he was the first-born and so should have taken his lot first, he was nevertheless delayed in taking his lot until Ephraim had taken first, and after that the lot came to the tribe of Manasseh; this was because of Yaakov’s blessing, which put Ephraim first in everything.
Machir, the first-born of Manasseh. That is, but among the sons of Manasseh, where there was no reason to put the younger before the first-born, the first-born took first.
The father of Gilead. He was called after his son Gilead; or it means “the ruler of Gilead,” named for what he later became.
A valiant warrior. And he chose to live across the Jordan on the frontier, in a dangerous place, to show the nations his strength; therefore Gilead and Bashan were his.
And now assignments were made. That is, after this the lot came to the remaining Manassites, to each clan.
The male descendants. Since this passage says that women of the Manassites also received a portion (verse 6), it says “the males” of their clans.
Our male kinsmen. That is, our father’s brothers.
In accordance with the L-rd’s instructions. By the word of the L-rd, at His command.
Ten districts fell to Manasseh. In the Land of Israel itself they took ten districts.

Manasseh’s daughters, etc. That is, since the daughters of Manasseh also received a portion, and the remaining sons of Manasseh took the land of Gilead, it was right and proper that in the Land of Israel itself they should take these ten districts, no fewer and no more, for this was the count due to them.

The boundary of Manasseh. The width from north to south ran from the border of the Asherites, who received their portion north of Manasseh, to Michmethath, which stood opposite the southwestern corner of Ephraim’s portion, facing Shechem, which belonged to Ephraim and stood in the southwestern corner.
The boundary continued. From west to east, on the north side.
To the right. It turned diagonally to the south and came to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The region of Tappuah. The places around Tappuah; but the town of Tappuah itself, although it stood within Manasseh’s border, belonged to Ephraim.

Then the boundary descended. That is, along the border that descended from Tappuah to the Wadi Kanah, south of the wadi mentioned above, those towns standing on that border belonged to Ephraim, although they stood among the towns of Manasseh, as was written above.
Ran on. The end of Manasseh’s border reached the Sea.
What lay to the south belonged to Ephraim. In the strip that the Josephites took, Ephraim took the south and Manasseh the north.
Its boundary. Manasseh’s.
With Asher. With the border of Asher.
Was contiguous. Manasseh with Asher, to the north of Manasseh.
On the east. For the portion of Issachar was by the Jordan, to the east of Manasseh.
Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh possessed, etc. Manasseh had towns inside the portions of Issachar and Asher that were near him.
Three regions. These towns stood in three districts.
Have you assigned as our portion. Lit. “given me”: to all the Josephites, Manasseh and Ephraim.
A single allotment. That is, a small portion, as if it were one lot and one district.
A numerous people. And this portion is not enough for me.
So greatly. Until I have multiplied, as you see.

Go up to the forest country. That is, if you are a numerous people, you can go up into the forest of the Perizzites and the Rephaim and cut down the trees to have a place to live; for if you were few, you would not have the strength to cut down so many forest trees, but since you are a numerous people, you can.
Seeing that you are cramped. If the hill country of Ephraim, for all its size, is too tight and narrow for you.
The hill country is not enough for us. It is true that the hill country of Ephraim is not enough for us.

Have iron chariots. That is, if you answer, “You also received the valley as your portion, and with it you have enough,” we will reply that the people of the valley are very strong, their charioteers are like iron, and they cannot be conquered.
Both those in Beth-shean, etc. He explains: these are the ones in Beth-shean, etc., which was given as Manasseh’s portion.
In the Valley of Jezreel. For Jezreel itself was in the portion of Issachar, and only the valley was in their portion.
You are indeed a numerous people. And so you have great strength to fight and widen your border, so that you will not have a small portion as if it were one lot.
The hill country shall be yours. That is, the forest on the hill that I mentioned will be yours without great effort, for it is forest land and there are not many people there to fight you.
You will clear it. You will cut down the trees to live there, and so its farthest limits will be yours, that is, the border going out from that hill and beyond.
You shall also dispossess. For by living on the hill you will easily be able to dispossess the Canaanites who live in the valley in Beth-shean, etc.

Even though they have iron chariots. Even though they have charioteers like iron and even though they are strong; for one who lives high up on the hill is much stronger than one who lives below in the valley.

The land was now under their control. From the time they set up the Tent of Meeting at Shiloh, which was in the portion of the Josephites, the L-rd helped them, and they conquered the land that they could not conquer before, as written above (17:12).
Which had not yet received. Because they did not yet know the borders of the land to divide them by lot.

Seven tribes. For five had already received their share: Moshe gave to the Reubenites, the Gadites and half of Manasseh (Num. 32:33), and Joshua gave to the Judites, the Ephraimites and half of Manasseh.

How long, etc., which … has assigned, etc. That is: I know your thoughts, why you do not send to write down the borders of the land and divide it — you think that if each knows his share, perhaps they will separate from one another and one will not fight for the other’s share. So he said: how long will your hands be slack? The L-rd is giving you the land, so even if one does not help the other, you will overcome them, for the L-rd will fight for you.
For purposes of apportionment. According to the number of shares that need to be assigned.

Into seven parts. For seven more tribes are to receive a portion: Judah remains to inherit its territory in the south of the Land of Israel, and the house of Joseph to inherit its territory in the north of what has already been conquered; and seven remain.
When you. That is, the messengers who go in place of all of you.

For the Levites have no share. He explains further why seven parts: the Levites have no share, and Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh have already received, etc., and Judah and the house of Joseph have the sixth share; so seven remain.
The priesthood of the L-rd. What is fitting for them to take for their priestly service.
The men. The messengers.
Joshua ordered. That is, he urged them on in this.
Town by town. According to the size of the towns: a large town against two small towns.
According to their divisions. According to the division described in the verses before us.
By their clans. Divided according to the clans.
On their northern rim. From east to west: the border began at the Jordan.
The northern flank. So Jericho was inside the border and belonged to Benjamin.
Into the hill country. This is the hill country of Bethel mentioned in the border of the Josephites.
Westward. Toward the west.
Ran on. The end of the border at this width; from there on the border line went inward and his portion grew narrower.
Southward. So Luz was not in Benjamin’s portion, but belonged to Ephraim.
That is, Bethel. For Yaakov called Luz Bethel, as it says in the Torah (Gen. 28:19); and this is not the Bethel near Ai, which was in Benjamin’s portion.
The hill south of Lower Beth-horon. So that too was not in his portion, but belonged to Ephraim.
The boundary now turned. The border went around on the western side from north to south.
From the hill. The border ran from the hill, etc., which stands in the north, went southward and ended at Kiriath-baal, that is Kiriath-jearim, on the northern border of Judah.
The southern rim. The southern border, from west to east, began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim.

Westward. Lit. “to the sea” — and this is not the Mediterranean Sea in the west; this sea was north of Judah, though it was not mentioned above; and so you will find in many places that something is mentioned in one place and not in another, although their borders were next to each other.
Then the boundary descended. For the fountain of the Waters of Nephtoah, which is Ein Eitam (Zevachim 54b, Rashi), was at the highest place in all the Land of Israel; so it says “descended.”
At … the Valley of Rephaim. The hill stood in the Valley of Rephaim, at its north.
Along the southern flank. Which stood on the flank of the Jebusites on the south; so the Jebusite city, that is Jerusalem, was in Benjamin’s portion.
Curving northward. The border came along the western side and went around En-rogel on its north; so it belonged to Judah.
Ran on to En-shemesh. From En-rogel it went out to En-shemesh.
To Geliloth. This is Gilgal, mentioned on the northern border of Judah; it was called by both names. At Gilgal the border went out to the south, and Benjamin’s portion grew wider.
It continued. From there it passed by the place called “facing the Arabah” on the north side; so it was not in Benjamin’s portion.
Into the Arabah. This is Beth-arabah, mentioned in Judah’s border, and the border was to its north.

Northern flank of Beth-hoglah. And it too was not in Benjamin’s portion. (The “Beth-hoglah” mentioned in Benjamin’s portion is another town with the same name.) “The tongue of the Dead Sea,” etc. — that is, where the Jordan falls into the Dead Sea, which is the southern end of the Jordan and the northern end of the sea.
That was the southern boundary. From west to east.
Was their boundary. It was a border for him on the eastern side.
According to its boundaries. The borders that enclose what was divided to all their clans.
By its clans. Divided by their clans.
Zela, Eleph. There are five towns in this verse: Zela the first, Eleph the second, Jerusalem the third, Gibeath the fourth, Kiriath the fifth.
Inside, etc. It was enclosed within Judah’s portion, inside the border described above.
Beer-sheba—or Sheba. This is one town, called by both names.
Ain, Rimmon. These are two towns: one is Ain, the other Rimmon.
Ramath-negeb. A high and elevated place on the south side.
Was part of the territory. From the district first given to the Judites they afterwards gave a portion to the Simeonites.
Since the share. For the portion first given to the Judites was more than was fitting for them; so the Simeonites received a portion among them.
At Sarid. Which stood at the end of the border of the Land of Israel, in the northwestern corner.
Their boundary ascended. From Sarid, along the western side, from north to south.
Westward. To the sea, and from there to Maralah, etc.
And it also ran from Sarid. The border turned back from Sarid to go from west to east along the northern side, and went along the territory of Chisloth-tabor, etc.
From there. From Japhia it passed southward, east of Gath-hepher; so that town was in Zebulun’s portion.
To Eth-kazin. That is, from the east of Gath-hepher it passed to Eth-kazin, which is the name of a place.
Where it curved to Neah. Which went around Neah.
Then it turned. This border went around Rimmon north of Hannathon, which stood north of Rimmon; so Rimmon, Hannathon and Neah belonged to Zebulun.
Its extreme limits. The end of the border at this width reached the Valley of Iphtah-el, which stood on the northern border of Asher.

Kattath, etc. That is, together with Kattath, etc., there were twelve; for in this verse he counted five towns, and seven of those he mentioned on the border; the rest belonged to the neighboring tribe.

Their territory comprised. The border ran by Jezreel, which was next to Manasseh’s portion, for the Valley of Jezreel belonged to Manasseh, as written above (17:16); “Chesulloth” — from Jezreel it went to Chesulloth, etc.

And Beth-shemesh. This is not the Beth-shemesh mentioned in the portion of Naphtali (verse 38), which lies north of Issachar, nor the one on the border of Judah (above 15:10). “Their boundary” is said of both borders, the northern and the southern: both ended at the Jordan.
Their boundary ran. The border went along the western side from south to north, to Helkath, etc.
And it touched. The border touched Carmel, which stands in the west.
It also ran. The border turned from west to east along the northern side and went to Beth-dagon.
Zebulun. The border of Zebulun, which was to its north.
And the Valley of Iphtah-el to the north. North of the Valley of Iphtah-el; so it was in Asher’s portion, and opposite it the width of Zebulun’s border ended, as written above.
Beth-emek. From the Valley of Iphtah-el the border came to Beth-emek, etc.
On the north. Lit. “on the left”: north of Cabul; so it belonged to Asher.
Ebron. From north of Cabul the border came to Ebron, etc.
The boundary turned. From Great Sidon the border went back from north to south, to Ramah, etc.
Then the boundary turned to Hosah. From the fortified city of Tyre the border went back from east to west, to Hosah.
To Mehebel, Achzib. For from Hosah the border came to the district of Achzib, and from there the border ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob. That is, together with these three towns, which did not stand on the border, he had twenty-two towns — these three and nineteen of those that stood on the border; the rest belonged to the tribe next to him.
The Naphtalites by their clans. What was divided to the Naphtalites, for each and every clan.
Their boundary ran. Their border went along the southern side, from west to east, from Heleph, etc.
The boundary then turned westward. The border went back from east to west along the northern side and came to Aznoth-tabor.
On the south. On the south of Zebulun, which is the north of Naphtali.
On the west. On the west of Naphtali, which is the east of Asher.

And Judah at the Jordan. And at the border of Judah it touched the Jordan, which stands in the east. For the northern border of Judah ended at the southern end of the Jordan, and Naphtali had the whole Jordan as its portion; so it touched the border of Judah at the end of the Jordan. The same is true of all the tribes whose border reached the Jordan; but he means to say that although Judah’s portion was at the southern end, it touched it too.
Its fortified towns. That is, these are the fortified towns of Naphtali: Ziddim, etc.
19 towns. That is, together with the fortified towns he had nineteen — sixteen fortified towns and three more of those that stood on the border; the rest belonged to the tribe next to him.
Zorah, Eshtaol. Perhaps these are not the ones on the border of Judah, and the portion of Dan was in the northwestern corner of Judah.
Ekron. This is not the one that was on the border of Judah.
At the border, etc. That is, those towns were part of Dan’s portion, together with the border opposite Joppa.

But the territory of the Danites slipped from their grasp. That is, the territory of Dan’s portion came out by lot smaller than they needed, and it was not enough for them; so afterwards they went up to fight Leshem. This is Laish, mentioned in the Book of Judges (18:7), and it was outside the border of the Land of Israel, not within it. (It was in the northeastern corner, opposite the portion of Naphtali; for our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bechorot 55a): the Jordan is so called because it descends (yored) from Dan, which is Leshem; and the Jordan begins in the northeastern corner. This is what Scripture says (I Kings 5:5): “from Dan to Beer-sheba,” meaning from one end of the Land of Israel to the other, diagonally; for Dan was in the northeastern corner and Beer-sheba in the southwestern corner, since it belonged to the portion of Simeon, which took that corner.)
Those towns. The ones mentioned above.
Allotting. Giving as a portion by lot.
By its boundaries. According to the borders described above.
At the command of the L-rd. They asked through the Urim and Thummim, and according to them they gave him the town he asked for, which is Timnath-serah.
Assigned. They gave Israel its portions by lot.
And the heads of the ancestral houses. The heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel.
By lot. This goes back to the beginning of the verse: “These are the portions that they assigned by lot.”
When they had finished dividing. They completed the division of the land by lot.
Designate. Lit. “for yourselves”: for your benefit.
As a refuge. To take in the manslayer from the hand of the blood avenger, so that he does not kill him while his heart is hot.
Plead his case. How he killed by mistake.
And they shall admit him. Even though they do not know that the truth is with him.
The blood avenger. A relative of the one who was killed, who wants to take revenge for him.
Pursue him. To his city of refuge.
They shall not hand … over. That is, the people of the town will help the manslayer and not hand him over to the blood avenger.
Since … without intent. If he killed without intent.
And had not been his enemy. Which would mean that he acted with cunning in the matter.
Stand trial. To judge him whether he must go into exile; and when he is found liable, he returns to his city of refuge and lives there until the high priest dies.
Thereafter. After the death of the high priest.
Before standing trial. Until he stands in judgment to be tried whether he deserves death; and if he is found guilty, then he is in the hand of the blood avenger to be put to death.
That we be given, etc. That is: and so, give them to us.
In accordance with the L-rd’s command. According to His commandment.
The following. Those listed below.
Among the Levites. Who were of the Levites, of the sons of Levi.
From the tribe of Judah. The lot came to them from the tribe of Judah, etc.

The remaining. For the descendants of Aharon, who were Kohathites, took from the tribe of Judah, etc.; and the remaining Kohathites — the descendants of Moshe and the descendants of Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel — took from the tribe of Ephraim, etc.
In Bashan. That is, the half that took its portion east of the Jordan, in the land of Bashan.
By their clans. Divided so that each clan would live in them by itself; it is explained in one place, and so in all of them.
By lot. Which of the tribes would give to which of the Levites.
Which will be listed. That is, further on in this section he will explain the names.
Among the … clans. Who were of the Kohathite clans.
For the first lot had fallen to them. That is, because the lot came to them first, they took first — not because of the dignity of the priesthood.
As his holding. As the share of his portion.
But to the descendants … they assigned. The whole number of these towns.
